masthead_title: Securing the Freehold for Everyone, Forever
masthead_lead: Our landmark community campaign to bring Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall Commons into permanent charitable ownership.

video_spotlight.headline: Watch the Community Movement in Action
video_spotlight.description: See our community standing together across Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall to secure 256 acres of ancient woodlands and sandstone rocks forever.

safeguards.heading: Why community ownership matters
safeguards.left_col: The Commons are protected by a range of legal and statutory safeguards, but ownership still matters. A private freeholder may have different priorities from those of the local community—particularly around public access, land management, and commercial pressures on the estate.
safeguards.right_col: Charitable community ownership ensures decisions are guided entirely by conservation and public enjoyment. Accountable to its members, local trustees, and the Charity Commission, the Friends would safeguard these historic green spaces for generations to come.

faqs.question: What happens now?
faqs.subtext: The marketing of the Commons as part of a wider estate
faqs.answer:
**The Commons are now being marketed as part of a wider estate that also includes The Pantiles.**

As this is a significantly different commercial proposition, the Friends will not be seeking to purchase the estate as currently offered, and there are no immediate plans to call on community pledges.

Our long-term ambition remains unchanged: to secure the Commons for the benefit of the community. We will continue to engage constructively with any future owner to explore opportunities for community ownership should they arise.

We will keep supporters informed of any significant developments.

faqs.question: Do pledges still matter?
faqs.subtext: How over 3,000 pledges demonstrate local mandate
faqs.answer:
**Yes.**

More than 3,000 residents have already pledged their support for community ownership. These pledges demonstrate the depth of community commitment to protecting the Commons for future generations.

Although the Friends are not seeking to purchase the estate in its current form, pledges remain an important expression of support should a future opportunity for community ownership arise.

faqs.question: Can I still make a pledge?
faqs.subtext: Submitting new pledges towards future acquisition
faqs.answer:
**Yes.**

New pledges are still welcome and help demonstrate continuing community support for ownership of the Commons by a local charity.

You can submit a pledge through our online form or by emailing [johnspbarber@gmail.com](mailto:johnspbarber@gmail.com).
